newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine 1997 wheat output seen 19 mln T.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine 1997 wheat output seen 19 mln T.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union, in association with Ukragroconsult, a private Ukrainian agricultural consultancy based in Kiev.
UKRAINE: WHEAT OUTPUT FORECAST IN 97 RAISED TO 19 MLN TONNES

MOSCOW, May 14 - Ukraine's total wheat production in 1997 is tentatively forecast at 19.3 million tonnes (or in a range of 18-20 million), up sharply from 1996's drought-hit crop of 13.55 million tonnes.
The recovery in wheat production will lead to an increase in Ukraine's wheat exports, although exports will fall well short of official government targets.

The government expects 1997/98 wheat exports to rise to five million tonnes. But this looks unlikely because of logistical problems, particularly stemming from obselete and inadequate port facilities.
In addition, Ukraine will have to replenish its heavily reduced wheat stocks.
SovEcon and Ukragroconsult therefore peg Ukraine's wheat exports in 1997/98 at about 1.5 million tonnes, compared with 0.65 million tonnes in 1996/97 after the 1996 crop failure.

Winter wheat in Ukraine accounts for the bulk of total wheat production in the country. The total wheat area harvested in 1997 is likely to increase to 6.25 million hectares, including 6.1 million hectares of winter wheat.
Favourable weather conditions have resulted in abnormally low winter-kill losses and benefited plantings' development this spring.
As at early May, winter wheat plantings in good condition with yield potential of about 5.5 tonnes per hectare were estimated at 58 percent of total winter wheat acreage.

Plantings in satisfactory condition with yield potential of about 3.5 tonnes per hectare accounted for 28 percent of the total. Plantings in poor condition with yield potential of about 2.0 tonnes per hectare made up the remaining 14 percent.

As a result, harvested winter wheat area and average yields in 1997 have been revised upwards from 5.9 to 6.1 million hectares and from 3.0 to 3.1 tonnes per hectare. This points to 1997 winter wheat output of 18.9 million tonnes.
SovEcon and Ukragroconsult's forecast for the 1997 spring wheat output remains unchanged at 0.36 million tonnes.
